text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Farm minister Jozias van Aartsen imposes pig breeding ban in areas hit by swine fever. (p1)
- Rabobank chairman Herman Wijffels casts doubt on 'textbook' start to monetary union, but says delay not an option. (p1)
- Ahold director Peter van Dun, president of its flagship supermarket chain Albert Heijn, to retire on October 1. (p3)
- Group of small shareholders in bio-tech firm MoGen rejects takeover bid by Britain's Zeneca as too low. (p3)
- Only a few Dutch pension funds use financial derivatives, study by sector regulator Verzekeringskamer shows. (p13)
- Justice minister Winnie Sorgdrager to study possibilities for new legislation enabling criminal proceedings against local authorities.(p3)
- Foreign minister Hans van Mierlo says counting on cooperation from the new French government in European treaty reform. (p5)
- Dutch energy companies slam proposals for new legislation to regulate energy sector. (p17)
- Government study indicates Schiphol Airport's emergency measures will not be able to cope with a major disaster (p1)
- Rotterdam seeking new identity as services hub with 240 million guilder economic transformation plan. (p3)
- Small businesses association MKB has a sound financial base. (p25)
- Chinese firm dismantling old steel smelter in IJmuiden could lose its permit due to bad working conditions. (p7) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Deutsche Telekom subsidiary T-Mobil criticizes traffic minister Annemarie Jorritsma for slow auctioning of mobile telecom licences. (p13)
